data.body:
Pre-sweep against origin/main 7927904a0 and tickets-branch 0b9294311b5. This plan's central number was stale in a way that would have inverted the epic's conclusion, so the Context, Approach, Scope, Testing and all acceptance criteria were rewritten. The title no longer pins a pair count, so it cannot go stale the same way again.

What was wrong. The plan said '51 known duplicate pairs identified in ticket eac3, of which 44 are semantic', and AC1 required benchmark.json to hold 51 pairs. eac3 did measure 51, honestly and by this exact method, but it measured 2,679 tickets and 43 recorded duplicates links. Running the plan's own stated procedure today over 5,663 live tickets finds 482 links closing into 148 clusters over 630 tickets, enumerating to 1,524 pairs. AC1 was therefore unsatisfiable by its own Approach: no implementation could follow 'exactly as eac3 did' and arrive at 51. Counting both archived and live tickets gives the same 1,524, so archiving does not explain the gap.

What the re-measurement found that matters more than the count. 1,431 of the 1,524 pairs -- 94 percent -- have byte-identical normalized titles. They sit in 84 clusters that are each a single repeated title; the largest is 12 copies of one bridge-state rotation ticket and the next is 9 copies of one comment-triage ticket. Those are bulk-creation artifacts, almost certainly a retry loop, not independently authored duplicates. Normalized-title matching scores about 100 percent recall on them. A benchmark that pooled all 1,524 pairs would therefore have reported near-perfect recall for the cheapest lexical candidate and rejected vector search -- on an artifact. That is the precise opposite of eac3's finding, which was that the duplicates worth catching are semantic: it measured 14 percent lexical recall because 44 of its 51 were semantic.

93 pairs have differing titles. That is the real benchmark, it is double eac3's 44, and it is the same kind of set. Spot-checked samples confirm the character: 'Attested snapshot fetch pulls unrelated oversized tickets branch' against 'Attested ref materialization broad-fetches all origin heads'; 'rebar doctor command' against 'rebar doctor: diagnose-and-heal health command'.

The rewrite keeps the story's intent -- choose a retrieval architecture on measurement -- and makes it measurable: the fixture stratifies every pair as lexical or semantic, recall is reported per stratum and never pooled, the semantic stratum is the decision criterion, and the lexical stratum is a control every candidate should near-saturate. The fixture records the tickets-branch SHA it was derived at, and --check re-derives the set at that SHA and refuses a fixture whose SHA is not an ancestor of current HEAD, so this specific staleness is now caught by the runner instead of by a reviewer.

Three further corrections, each measured rather than assumed:
- Scope said the top-level evals/ tree is created by the eval-harness epic's corpus-move story and that this story depends on it. That dependency has landed: evals/ was created by commit 91d39fd6061, 'Move research corpus out of docs to evals/'. Restated as completed work.
- Candidate 2 pointed at the retired ticket_digest prompt via 'the commit before its removal, recorded on the closing comment of the removal story under epic bossy-skittish-foal' -- an indirection through a comment that may or may not carry the SHA. Measured directly: the prompt was deleted by 2de5f341ec4, so it is readable at parent f147e08242f, where it lives in src/rebar/llm/contracts.py and src/rebar/llm/overlap/. The SHA is now named in the plan.
- Candidate 3 said boto3 is provided by the bedrock extra. The extra is pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock], which pulls boto3 transitively; boto3 1.43.68 imports in the worktree venv. Reworded to state the actual path rather than imply a direct dependency.

Verified correct and left alone: rebar list --full exists and is accepted; rebar.toml carries [llm] bedrock_region_name = us-east-1 at :213; scripts/check_adr_numbers.py and scripts/gen_adr_index.py both exist; docs/ticket-model.md documents the duplicates relation at :136 and :143. This ticket has no blockers, so it is reviewable now.
